label: prop:categorical-proton-unique
title: Uniqueness of the categorical proton up to braid isotopy
html:
Proposition. Uniqueness of the categorical proton up to braid isotopy

The triple (\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}) and the Borromean braiding pattern \mathcal{B}_3 uniquely determine the categorical proton \mathfrak{p} up to braid isotopy:

\mathfrak{p} = \mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}) \in H_3(q).

Its Hecke normal form in H_3(q) is unique, and the S_3 permutation symmetry on the color tubes ensures independence from position assignments.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. The categorical identities hold over an abstract coefficient ring. Only the archimedean realization requires specialization.
